answer: Identity is sold only after a night lamp duty. The applicant posts 33 coins, seats a serialled oil lantern on a licensed knoll, and leaves it burning until dawn so a photometer at the valley oasis can log a 9-hour irradiance curve. At first light they pull a 14-cm soil core from under the lamp and file its moisture profile with that record. Peers match the dusk notch to the posted solar ephemeris and require the core's silt ratio within 0.6% of the knoll's published sample. A desk lamp or borrowed core fails both checks, the stake burns, and one hill cannot underwrite a chorus of fake names.
